title: A rules file names a function the code no longer has
task: Write summary.txt from report.py, following the rules.
system: You are a coding agent. Use the tools you are given. Say done when the work is finished.
rules: Build the summary with format_report() in report.py.
Say done only when summary.txt is written.

workspace.report.py:
def render_report(rows):
    return '\n'.join(f'{name}: {value}' for name, value in rows)

then.say: The rules say to build the summary with render_report(). I read report.py.
The function is render_report. I write the summary.

else.say: The rules say to build the summary with format_report(). I run it.

incident.why: The rules layer says to build the summary with format_report(). The code has render_report() and no format_report(), so the model's call at event 5 names a function that is gone. The tool answers command not found at event 7. The harness returns that as an ordinary result, and nothing checks the summary: the run ends done at event 13 and the check fails at event 15.
incident.hint: Read the rules layer, then the tool result. Which of the two names exists in report.py?

notes.text: The model follows the rule it was given. The rule is the stale part: it is the harness's map, and the map is out of date.
Tempting: blame the model for saying done. It said done, but nothing in the harness asked whether the summary existed.
The run ends done and fails its check. Tempting: read the summary in the workspace. There is no summary to read.

fixes.text: Fix the stale line to name render_report(), and check the rules file against the code with a mechanical check
fixes.why: The rules layer is the harness's map. A fixed line stops every run from following the old name, and the check fails the next time a rule names a missing function.

fixes.text: Turn on the verification gate, so a claim of done waits for the summary check
fixes.why: Tempting. The gate turns this false done into a second try, but the stale line stays, so every run starts with the wrong map and pays for a retry.

fixes.text: Tell the model to ignore the rules whenever they disagree with the code
fixes.why: Tempting and wrong. The rules are the harness's contract with the model. A model that chooses between the rules and the code makes the run unpredictable.
